sanskrit: anvīyamāno vīreṇa dāśārheṇa mahātmanā yuyudhānena ca tathā tathaiva ca yuyutsunā
english: He was followed by the hero of the Dāśārha line, the great-souled one, and by Yuyudhāna as well, and likewise by Yuyutsu.

sanskrit: tam anvagāt suduḥkhārtā draupadī śokakarśitā saha pāñcālayoṣidbhir yās tatrāsan samāgatāḥ
english: Behind him went Draupadī, stricken with deep sorrow and wasted by grief, together with the women of Pāñcāla who had gathered there.

sanskrit: sa gaṅgām anu vṛndāni strīṇāṃ bharatasattama kurarīṇām ivārtānāṃ krośantīnāṃ dadarśa ha
english: Along the Gaṅgā, O best of the Bhāratas, he beheld throngs of women crying out in their anguish like grieving ospreys.

sanskrit: tābhiḥ parivṛto rājā rudatībhiḥ sahasraśaḥ ūrdhvabāhubhir ārtābhir bruvatībhiḥ priyāpriye
english: The king was surrounded by those weeping women in their thousands, who with arms upraised and stricken with grief spoke words both kind and bitter.

sanskrit: kva nu dharmajñatā rājñaḥ kva nu sādyānṛśaṃsatā yadāvadhīt pitṝn bhrātṝn gurūn putrān sakhīn api
english: Where now is the king's knowledge of dharma, where now his gentle compassion, when he has slain fathers, brothers, elders, sons, and even friends?

sanskrit: ghātayitvā kathaṃ droṇaṃ bhīṣmaṃ cāpi pitāmaham manas te 'bhūn mahābāho hatvā cāpi jayadratham
english: Having brought about the deaths of Droṇa and of Bhīṣma the grandsire, how was your heart set at ease, O mighty-armed one, even after slaying Jayadratha?

sanskrit: kiṃ nu rājyena te kāryaṃ pitṝn bhrātṝn apaśyataḥ abhimanyuṃ ca durdharṣaṃ draupadeyāṃś ca bhārata
english: What use is the kingdom to you, who no longer behold your fathers and brothers, nor the unconquerable Abhimanyu, nor the sons of Draupadī, O Bhārata?

sanskrit: atītya tā mahābāhuḥ krośantīḥ kurarīr iva vavande pitaraṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Passing beyond those women who wailed like ospreys, the mighty-armed Yudhiṣṭhira, the Dharma-king, paid homage to his elder, the father of his house.

sanskrit: tato 'bhivādya pitaraṃ dharmeṇāmitrakarśanāḥ nyavedayanta nāmāni pāṇḍavās te 'pi sarvaśaḥ
english: Then, having saluted their father according to custom, those Pāṇḍavas, harriers of their foes, announced their names, each one in turn.

sanskrit: tam ātmajāntakaraṇaṃ pitā putravadhārditaḥ aprīyamāṇaḥ śokārtaḥ pāṇḍavaṃ pariṣasvaje
english: That father, tormented by the slaughter of his sons, with no gladness in his heart and worn by grief, embraced the Pāṇḍava who had brought about the end of his offspring.

sanskrit: dharmarājaṃ pariṣvajya sāntvayitvā ca bhārata duṣṭātmā bhīmam anvaicchad didhakṣur iva pāvakaḥ
english: Having embraced the Dharma-king and consoled him, O Bhārata, the evil-minded one sought out Bhīma, like a fire eager to consume him.

sanskrit: sa kopapāvakas tasya śokavāyusamīritaḥ bhīmasenamayaṃ dāvaṃ didhakṣur iva dṛśyate
english: The fire of his wrath, fanned by the wind of his grief, appeared as though it would burn up a forest that was Bhīmasena himself.

sanskrit: tasya saṃkalpam ājñāya bhīmaṃ praty aśubhaṃ hariḥ bhīmam ākṣipya pāṇibhyāṃ pradadau bhīmam āyasam
english: Perceiving his malign intent against Bhīma, Hari drew Bhīma aside with his hands and set before the king an iron Bhīma in his place.

sanskrit: prāg eva tu mahābuddhir buddhvā tasyeṅgitaṃ hariḥ saṃvidhānaṃ mahāprājñas tatra cakre janārdanaḥ
english: For Hari of great intellect, having read the old man's intent beforehand, the deeply wise Janārdana had already made his arrangement there.

sanskrit: taṃ tu gṛhyaiva pāṇibhyāṃ bhīmasenam ayasmayam babhañja balavān rājā manyamāno vṛkodaram
english: Seizing that Bhīmasena made of iron with both his hands, the mighty king shattered it, believing it to be Vṛkodara.

sanskrit: nāgāyutabalaprāṇaḥ sa rājā bhīmam āyasam bhaṅktvā vimathitoraskaḥ susrāva rudhiraṃ mukhāt
english: That king, whose strength of breath was as that of ten thousand elephants, having broken the iron Bhīma, his chest crushed in the effort, spat blood from his mouth.

sanskrit: tataḥ papāta medinyāṃ tathaiva rudhirokṣitaḥ prapuṣpitāgraśikharaḥ pārijāta iva drumaḥ
english: Then he fell upon the earth, drenched in blood, like a pārijāta tree whose topmost crown is in full flower.

sanskrit: paryagṛhṇata taṃ vidvān sūto gāvalgaṇis tadā maivam ity abravīc cainaṃ śamayan sāntvayann iva
english: The wise sūta, the son of Gavalgaṇa, then took hold of him and said, "Not so!", calming and consoling him.

sanskrit: sa tu kopaṃ samutsṛjya gatamanyur mahāmanāḥ hā hā bhīmeti cukrośa bhūyaḥ śokasamanvitaḥ
english: And he, the high-minded one, casting off his wrath, his anger now spent, cried out again, "Alas, alas, Bhīma!", overcome once more with grief.

sanskrit: taṃ viditvā gatakrodhaṃ bhīmasenavadhārditam vāsudevo varaḥ puṃsām idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Knowing his wrath had passed and that he was tormented at the supposed slaying of Bhīmasena, Vāsudeva, the foremost of men, spoke these words.

sanskrit: mā śuco dhṛtarāṣṭra tvaṃ naiṣa bhīmas tvayā hataḥ āyasī pratimā hy eṣā tvayā rājan nipātitā
english: "Grieve not, Dhṛtarāṣṭra; this is no Bhīma you have slain. It was an iron image, O king, that you have struck down.

sanskrit: tvāṃ krodhavaśam āpannaṃ viditvā bharatarṣabha mayāpakṛṣṭaḥ kaunteyo mṛtyor daṃṣṭrāntaraṃ gataḥ
english: Knowing you had fallen under the sway of wrath, O bull of the Bhāratas, I drew the son of Kuntī away, though he had passed between the very fangs of death.

sanskrit: na hi te rājaśārdūla bale tulyo 'sti kaś cana kaḥ saheta mahābāho bāhvor nigrahaṇaṃ naraḥ
english: For there is none, O tiger among kings, who is your equal in strength. What man, O mighty-armed one, could endure the grip of your arms?

sanskrit: yathāntakam anuprāpya jīvan kaś cin na mucyate evaṃ bāhvantaraṃ prāpya tava jīven na kaś cana
english: As none who comes upon Death escapes alive, so none who falls within the compass of your arms could live.

sanskrit: tasmāt putreṇa yā sā te pratimā kāritāyasī bhīmasya seyaṃ kauravya tavaivopahṛtā mayā
english: Therefore that iron image of Bhīma which your son had fashioned, this very one, O Kauravya, I set before you in his stead.

sanskrit: putraśokābhisaṃtāpād dharmād apahṛtaṃ manaḥ tava rājendra tena tvaṃ bhīmasenaṃ jighāṃsasi
english: Through the torment of grief for your sons, your mind has been drawn away from dharma, O lord of kings, and so you sought to slay Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: na ca te tat kṣamaṃ rājan hanyās tvaṃ yad vṛkodaram na hi putrā mahārāja jīveyus te kathaṃ cana
english: Nor would it be fitting for you, O king, that you should slay Vṛkodara; for your sons, O great king, can in no way be brought back to life.

sanskrit: tasmād yat kṛtam asmābhir manyamānaiḥ kṣamaṃ prati anumanyasva tat sarvaṃ mā ca śoke manaḥ kṛthāḥ
english: Therefore approve of all that we have done, judging it fitting, and do not set your heart upon grief."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tata enam upātiṣṭhañ śaucārthaṃ paricārakāḥ kṛtaśaucaṃ punaś cainaṃ provāca madhusūdanaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then the attendants came to him to perform his cleansing, and when his cleansing was done, the slayer of Madhu addressed him once more.

sanskrit: rājann adhītā vedās te śāstrāṇi vividhāni ca śrutāni ca purāṇāni rājadharmāś ca kevalāḥ
english: "O king, you have studied the Vedas and the manifold treatises, you have heard the ancient lore, and the very duties of kings.

sanskrit: evaṃ vidvān mahāprājña nākārṣīr vacanaṃ tadā pāṇḍavān adhikāñ jānan bale śaurye ca kaurava
english: Yet though so learned, O greatly wise one, you did not then heed counsel, O Kaurava, even knowing the Pāṇḍavas superior in strength and valor.

sanskrit: rājā hi yaḥ sthiraprajñaḥ svayaṃ doṣān avekṣate deśakālavibhāgaṃ ca paraṃ śreyaḥ sa vindati
english: For the king who is steadfast in wisdom, who himself examines his faults and the divisions of place and time, attains the highest good.

sanskrit: ucyamānaṃ ca yaḥ śreyo gṛhṇīte no hitāhite āpadaṃ samanuprāpya sa śocaty anaye sthitaḥ
english: But he who, when the good is told to him, does not grasp what helps and what harms, comes upon calamity and grieves, fixed in misrule.

sanskrit: tato 'nyavṛttam ātmānaṃ samavekṣasva bhārata rājaṃs tvaṃ hy avidheyātmā duryodhanavaśe sthitaḥ
english: Now therefore look upon yourself, who took to another course, O Bhārata; for you, O king, were ungoverned in spirit and stood under Duryodhana's sway.

sanskrit: ātmāparādhād āyastas tat kiṃ bhīmaṃ jighāṃsasi tasmāt saṃyaccha kopaṃ tvaṃ svam anusmṛtya duṣkṛtam
english: Afflicted through your own fault, why then do you seek to slay Bhīma? Therefore restrain your wrath, remembering your own misdeed.

sanskrit: yas tu tāṃ spardhayā kṣudraḥ pāñcālīm ānayat sabhām sa hato bhīmasenena vairaṃ praticikīrṣatā
english: He who in his baseness, out of rivalry, dragged the princess of Pāñcāla into the assembly hall, he was slain by Bhīmasena, who sought to requite the enmity.

sanskrit: ātmano 'tikramaṃ paśya putrasya ca durātmanaḥ yad anāgasi pāṇḍūnāṃ parityāgaḥ paraṃtapa
english: Look upon the transgression of yourself and of your evil-souled son, in that the sons of Pāṇḍu were cast off though guiltless, O scorcher of foes."

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ sa kṛṣṇena sarvaṃ satyaṃ janādhipa uvāca devakīputraṃ dhṛtarāṣṭro mahīpatiḥ
english: Thus addressed by Kṛṣṇa, all of it true, O lord of men, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the ruler of the earth, spoke to the son of Devakī.

sanskrit: evam etan mahābāho yathā vadasi mādhava putrasnehas tu dharmātman dhairyān māṃ samacālayat
english: "So it is, O mighty-armed one, even as you say, O Mādhava; but love for my sons, O righteous one, shook me from my firmness.

sanskrit: diṣṭyā tu puruṣavyāghro balavān satyavikramaḥ tvadgupto nāgamat kṛṣṇa bhīmo bāhvantaraṃ mama
english: By good fortune that tiger among men, the mighty Bhīma of true valor, guarded by you, O Kṛṣṇa, did not come within the compass of my arms.

sanskrit: idānīṃ tv aham ekāgro gatamanyur gatajvaraḥ madhyamaṃ pāṇḍavaṃ vīraṃ spraṣṭum icchāmi keśava
english: But now, single-minded, my anger gone and my fever stilled, I wish to touch the middle Pāṇḍava, that hero, O Keśava."

sanskrit: hateṣu pārthivendreṣu putreṣu nihateṣu ca pāṇḍuputreṣu me śarma prītiś cāpy avatiṣṭhate
english: "With the lords of the earth slain and my sons struck down, in the sons of Pāṇḍu my refuge and my affection now abide."

sanskrit: tataḥ sa bhīmaṃ ca dhanaṃjayaṃ ca; mādryāś ca putrau puruṣapravīrau pasparśa gātraiḥ prarudan sugātrān; āśvāsya kalyāṇam uvāca cainān
english: Then, weeping, he touched with his own limbs the fair-bodied Bhīma and Dhanaṃjaya and the two sons of Mādrī, those foremost of heroes among men; and comforting them, he spoke kind words to them.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca dhṛtarāṣṭrābhyanujñātās tatas te kurupuṃgavāḥ abhyayur bhrātaraḥ sarve gāndhārīṃ sahakeśavāḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then, with Dhṛtarāṣṭra's leave, those bulls among the Kurus, all the brothers together with Keśava, went forth to Gāndhārī.

sanskrit: tato jñātvā hatāmitraṃ dharmarājaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram gāndhārī putraśokārtā śaptum aicchad aninditā
english: Then Gāndhārī, the blameless one, stricken with grief for her sons, on learning that Yudhiṣṭhira the Dharma-king had slain his foes, wished to curse him.

sanskrit: tasyāḥ pāpam abhiprāyaṃ viditvā pāṇḍavān prati ṛṣiḥ satyavatīputraḥ prāg eva samabudhyata
english: Discerning her baleful intent against the Pāṇḍavas, the seer, the son of Satyavatī, had already understood it beforehand.

sanskrit: sa gaṅgāyām upaspṛśya puṇyagandhaṃ payaḥ śuci taṃ deśam upasaṃpede paramarṣir manojavaḥ
english: Having touched in the Gaṅgā its pure, sweet-scented water, that supreme seer, swift as thought, came to that place.

sanskrit: divyena cakṣuṣā paśyan manasānuddhatena ca sarvaprāṇabhṛtāṃ bhāvaṃ sa tatra samabudhyata
english: Seeing with his divine eye and with a mind unagitated, he there understood the inmost feeling of all living beings.

sanskrit: sa snuṣām abravīt kāle kalyavādī mahātapāḥ śāpakālam avākṣipya śamakālam udīrayan
english: That great ascetic, speaker of fair words, spoke to his daughter-in-law at the fitting moment, turning aside the time of cursing and calling forth the time of peace.

sanskrit: na kopaḥ pāṇḍave kāryo gāndhāri śamam āpnuhi rajo nigṛhyatām etac chṛṇu cedaṃ vaco mama
english: "No wrath should be turned upon the Pāṇḍava, O Gāndhārī; attain to peace. Let this passion be restrained, and hear these words of mine.

sanskrit: uktāsy aṣṭādaśāhāni putreṇa jayam icchatā śivam āśāssva me mātar yudhyamānasya śatrubhiḥ
english: For eighteen days your son, longing for victory, said to you, 'Wish me well, mother, as I fight against my foes.'

sanskrit: sā tathā yācyamānā tvaṃ kāle kāle jayaiṣiṇā uktavaty asi gāndhāri yato dharmas tato jayaḥ
english: And you, thus entreated time and again by him who longed for victory, said, O Gāndhārī, 'Where dharma is, there is victory.'

sanskrit: na cāpy atītāṃ gāndhāri vācaṃ te vitathām aham smarāmi bhāṣamāṇāyās tathā praṇihitā hy asi
english: Nor, O Gāndhārī, do I recall a single word once uttered by you proving false as you spoke, so resolutely fixed have you been.

sanskrit: sā tvaṃ dharmaṃ parismṛtya vācā coktvā manasvini kopaṃ saṃyaccha gāndhāri maivaṃ bhūḥ satyavādini
english: Therefore, calling dharma to mind and that word you yourself spoke, O high-minded one, restrain your wrath, O Gāndhārī; be not thus, O speaker of truth."

sanskrit: gāndhāry uvāca bhagavan nābhyasūyāmi naitān icchāmi naśyataḥ putraśokena tu balān mano vihvalatīva me
english: Gāndhārī said: "Blessed one, I bear them no ill will, nor do I wish these to perish; but through grief for my sons my mind is, as it were, violently distraught."

sanskrit: yathaiva kuntyā kaunteyā rakṣitavyās tathā mayā yathaiva dhṛtarāṣṭreṇa rakṣitavyās tathā mayā
english: "Even as the sons of Kuntī are to be guarded by Kuntī, so are they to be guarded by me; even as they are to be guarded by Dhṛtarāṣṭra, so by me.

sanskrit: duryodhanāparādhena śakuneḥ saubalasya ca karṇaduḥśāsanābhyāṃ ca vṛtto 'yaṃ kurusaṃkṣayaḥ
english: Through the offense of Duryodhana, and of Śakuni the son of Subala, and of Karṇa and Duḥśāsana, has this destruction of the Kurus come to pass.

sanskrit: nāparādhyati bībhatsur na ca pārtho vṛkodaraḥ nakulaḥ sahadevo vā naiva jātu yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Bībhatsu does no wrong, nor does Pārtha Vṛkodara, nor Nakula nor Sahadeva, nor ever Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: yudhyamānā hi kauravyāḥ kṛntamānāḥ parasparam nihatāḥ sahitāś cānyais tatra nāsty apriyaṃ mama
english: For the Kurus, fighting and cutting one another down, were slain together with others; in that I find nothing to grieve me.

sanskrit: yat tu karmākarod bhīmo vāsudevasya paśyataḥ duryodhanaṃ samāhūya gadāyuddhe mahāmanāḥ
english: But that deed which the high-minded Bhīma did in the sight of Vāsudeva, when he challenged Duryodhana to combat with the mace—

sanskrit: śikṣayābhyadhikaṃ jñātvā carantaṃ bahudhā raṇe adho nābhyāṃ prahṛtavāṃs tan me kopam avardhayat
english: knowing him the better in skill as he ranged in many ways through the fight, he struck him below the navel—that has swelled my wrath.

sanskrit: kathaṃ nu dharmaṃ dharmajñaiḥ samuddiṣṭaṃ mahātmabhiḥ tyajeyur āhave śūrāḥ prāṇahetoḥ kathaṃ cana
english: How could heroes ever forsake in battle, for the sake of their own lives, the dharma laid down by the great-souled knowers of dharma?"

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tac chrutvā vacanaṃ tasyā bhīmaseno 'tha bhītavat gāndhārīṃ pratyuvācedaṃ vacaḥ sānunayaṃ tadā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hearing that speech of hers, Bhīmasena then, as though afraid, answered Gāndhārī with these conciliatory words.

sanskrit: adharmo yadi vā dharmas trāsāt tatra mayā kṛtaḥ ātmānaṃ trātukāmena tan me tvaṃ kṣantum arhasi
english: "Whether it was unrighteous or righteous, it was done by me there out of fear, in my wish to save myself; for that you ought to forgive me.

sanskrit: na hi yuddhena putras te dharmeṇa sa mahābalaḥ śakyaḥ kena cid udyantum ato viṣamam ācaram
english: For that mighty son of yours could not be overcome by anyone in fair fight by lawful means; therefore I acted unfairly.

sanskrit: sainyasyaiko 'vaśiṣṭo 'yaṃ gadāyuddhe ca vīryavān māṃ hatvā na hared rājyam iti caitat kṛtaṃ mayā
english: He alone of the army was left, and valiant in combat with the mace; lest by slaying me he carry off the kingdom, this was done by me.

sanskrit: rājaputrīṃ ca pāñcālīm ekavastrāṃ rajasvalām bhavatyā viditaṃ sarvam uktavān yat sutas tava
english: And the princess of Pāñcāla, in a single garment and in her courses—you yourself know all that your son said to her.

sanskrit: suyodhanam asaṃgṛhya na śakyā bhūḥ sasāgarā kevalā bhoktum asmābhir ataś caitat kṛtaṃ mayā
english: Without overpowering Suyodhana, the earth with its seas could not be ours alone to enjoy; therefore this was done by me.

sanskrit: tac cāpy apriyam asmākaṃ putras te samupācarat draupadyā yat sabhāmadhye savyam ūrum adarśayat
english: This too your son did against us, a hateful thing, when in the midst of the assembly he bared his left thigh to Draupadī.

sanskrit: tatraiva vadhyaḥ so 'smākaṃ durācāro 'mba te sutaḥ dharmarājājñayā caiva sthitāḥ sma samaye tadā
english: Even then that ill-conducted son of yours, O mother, deserved death at our hands; but at the Dharma-king's command we then abided by the compact.

sanskrit: vairam uddhukṣitaṃ rājñi putreṇa tava tan mahat kleśitāś ca vane nityaṃ tata etat kṛtaṃ mayā
english: That great enmity was kindled by your son, O queen, and we were continually tormented in the forest; therefore this was done by me.

sanskrit: vairasyāsya gataḥ pāraṃ hatvā duryodhanaṃ raṇe rājyaṃ yudhiṣṭhiraḥ prāpto vayaṃ ca gatamanyavaḥ
english: By slaying Duryodhana in battle I have reached the far shore of this enmity; Yudhiṣṭhira has gained the kingdom, and our anger is gone."

sanskrit: gāndhāry uvāca na tasyaiṣa vadhas tāta yat praśaṃsasi me sutam kṛtavāṃś cāpi tat sarvaṃ yad idaṃ bhāṣase mayi
english: Gāndhārī said: "This is no slaying of his, dear child, though you praise my son to me; and he did indeed do all that you now tell me of.

sanskrit: hatāśve nakule yat tad vṛṣasenena bhārata apibaḥ śoṇitaṃ saṃkhye duḥśāsanaśarīrajam
english: But when Nakula's horse had been slain by Vṛṣasena, O Bhārata, in the battle you drank the blood that sprang from Duḥśāsana's body.

sanskrit: sadbhir vigarhitaṃ ghoram anāryajanasevitam krūraṃ karmākaroḥ kasmāt tad ayuktaṃ vṛkodara
english: You did a cruel deed, abhorred by the good, dreadful, such as only the ignoble practice—why this unseemly act, O Vṛkodara?"

sanskrit: bhīmasena uvāca anyasyāpi na pātavyaṃ rudhiraṃ kiṃ punaḥ svakam yathaivātmā tathā bhrātā viśeṣo nāsti kaś cana
english: Bhīmasena said: "Even another's blood is not to be drunk, how much less one's own; but as is oneself, so is a brother—there is no difference whatever.

sanskrit: rudhiraṃ na vyatikrāmad dantoṣṭhaṃ me 'mba mā śucaḥ vaivasvatas tu tad veda hastau me rudhirokṣitau
english: The blood did not pass beyond my teeth and lips, O mother; grieve not. The son of Vivasvat knows that—only my hands were stained with blood.

sanskrit: hatāśvaṃ nakulaṃ dṛṣṭvā vṛṣasenena saṃyuge bhrātṝṇāṃ saṃprahṛṣṭānāṃ trāsaḥ saṃjanito mayā
english: Seeing Nakula's horse slain by Vṛṣasena in the battle, I sought thereby to strike terror into the brothers who had been exulting against us.

sanskrit: keśapakṣaparāmarśe draupadyā dyūtakārite krodhād yad abruvaṃ cāhaṃ tac ca me hṛdi vartate
english: What I said in wrath when Draupadī's braid of hair was seized, brought about by the gambling, that too still abides in my heart.

sanskrit: kṣatradharmāc cyuto rājñi bhaveyaṃ śāsvatīḥ samāḥ pratijñāṃ tām anistīrya tatas tat kṛtavān aham
english: I should have fallen from the duty of a kṣatriya for everlasting years, O queen, had I not fulfilled that vow; therefore I did the deed."
